solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Orbital motion covering only 40 per cent of orbit is a chaotic situation

indicators.note: forty per cent of a five-letter word is two letters, so only the opening two are kept
one thing covering another wraps around it, so the outer term is split to hold the inner

blocks.note: a satellite in orbit is in continuous free fall around the planet
the first two of its five letters

explanation.surface: A science lesson on orbits turns into a description of a messy scene.
explanation.walkthrough: FREE(OR)FALL: the two letters sit between the halves of the orbital term.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorderly brawl or contest in which anyone may join, a chaotic situation.

clue.text: Melee to become untidy at the edges

blocks.note: first meaning: a noisy fight or brawl
second meaning: what worn cloth does as threads loosen

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a scrum getting ragged; the two halves are separate meanings, noun and verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a fight or skirmish, and fabric frays when its threads unravel at the edge.

clue.text: Intellectual urge picked up with professor finally leaving

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word
a letter that is leaving goes away from the word it was in

blocks.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
something heard has been picked up by ear; a synonym, not a sound-alike
its final letter

explanation.surface: An academic prodded into action once the professor has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: HEARD loses its R to leave HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is an informal, often mocking name for a bookish intellectual.

clue.text: Join the ranks, leading line with excellent resolve

blocks.note: soldiers fall in when they line up in formation
top means foremost, leading
L is the abbreviation for line
ace means first-rate

explanation.surface: A recruit lines up, at the head of the line, with fine determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' reads as a noun, determination, but is the verb, to sort itself out.
explanation.definitionFit: When things fall into place they resolve themselves and become clear or settled.

clue.text: Stay on the left?

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
the left is one side, a definition by example, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Asking whether to remain on the left, of a road or of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'the left' is only one example of a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or stay somewhere, especially permanently.

clue.text: Excellent litre, supported by University expert in beer

indicators.note: in a down entry a thing supported by another sits on top of it, so it comes first
in places the preceding letters inside the drink

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for litre
ale is a type of beer
U is the abbreviation for university
a dab hand is an expert

explanation.surface: Praise for a litre of good ale from a university brewing expert.
explanation.walkthrough: L + A(U + DAB)LE. 'Dab' is British usage, from 'dab hand', a skilled person.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudable means deserving praise, so commendable or excellent.

clue.text: Fine American vessel in trouble

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
USS (United States Ship) prefixes the names of American naval vessels

explanation.surface: A US ship has run into difficulties but is otherwise in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking trouble over something and making a fuss of it are close synonyms for bother.

clue.text: Crashed out, instrument not entirely ideal

indicators.note: something crashed is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled
not entirely means a word appears without its last part

blocks.note: taken as written
a piano is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A musician has crashed out of a contest with a less-than-perfect performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian means idealistic or describing a perfect society, as in Thomas More's Utopia.

clue.text: Restaged musical with unusual superficial likeness

indicators.note: a restaged show is put on in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A theatre revives a show in an odd new production that only resembles the original.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulacrum is an image or imitation that has the appearance of something without its substance.

clue.text: Knight set to participate in Australian service

indicators.note: participating in something means going inside it, so these letters are placed within the other term

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Australian
N is the chess notation for a knight
to set as jelly does is to gel

explanation.surface: A knight is about to take part in a church service down under.
explanation.walkthrough: A(N + GEL)US: knight and set join and go inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion commemorating the Incarnation, recited morning, noon and evening at the ringing of a bell.

clue.text: Radio operator's character is unvarying

blocks.note: first meaning: the code word for the letter U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
second meaning: the same throughout

explanation.surface: Someone on the radio has a dull, monotonous personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like personality but means a letter of the alphabet, as spelt out by radio operators.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means constant and the same in all cases, and the noun names the spoken signal for U.

clue.text: Uncertain blend of tea and dinnertime

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A confusion between tea and dinner, the British debate over what to call the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeterminate means not fixed or not exactly known, so uncertain.

clue.text: Late supporting worker

blocks.note: to be behind someone is to back them
a hand is a manual labourer

explanation.surface: A recently deceased backer of labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means behind schedule or in arrears, so late.

clue.text: Wrong book removed from account

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, leaving the remainder

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a bill is an account of money owed

explanation.surface: A ledger entry has been wrongly taken out of the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as an adjective or noun means bad or wrong, as in ill deeds.

clue.text: Study that involves European city coming in second?

definitions.text: Study that involves European city coming in second?

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or enclose, so the study word holds the rest
coming in means entering, so the city goes inside the short time unit

blocks.note: to con is to study or pore over
a mo is a moment, a second
Paris is the French capital

explanation.surface: A survey in which a European city ranks as runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mo' is British slang for a moment, and 'con' is an old word for study. The whole clue also defines: ranking a city second implies comparing it with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranking a city second only makes sense when it is measured against others, which is what a comparative study does.

clue.text: What's rum? "Alcoholic drink without head" should capture it

indicators.note: with no head means the opening letter of the drink is dropped
capturing something means holding it inside, so the word goes within the shortened drink

blocks.note: a toddy is a hot drink of spirits, sugar and water
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle about rum, answered by a quote about a headless drink that holds it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the spirit, matching the drink theme, but here it is the British adjective for strange. ODD(IT)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum in British slang means strange, and an oddity is a strange thing.

clue.text: Funny caption about Liberal not motivated by sex?

indicators.note: something funny is peculiar or odd, so these letters come out in a strange order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A cartoon caption about a Liberal politician that is joking but not saucy.
explanation.definitionFit: A platonic relationship is affectionate but without sexual desire.

clue.text: Son ignoring encouragement to drink not coming from senior level

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the phrase

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
bottoms up is a toast urging people to drain their glasses

explanation.surface: A son who will not join in the toasts at a company do, and is not the boss's choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottom-up approach starts from the lower ranks rather than being imposed by management.

clue.text: Dishonest scheme giving house to patient fellow

blocks.note: to house a guest is to put them up
Job is the Biblical figure famous for his patience

explanation.surface: A crooked plan involving lodging a long-suffering man.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverbial 'patience of Job' comes from the Old Testament book.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a fraud arranged beforehand, such as a rigged result.

clue.text: Bow of vessel that's raised speed at sea

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pot is a vessel
a knot is a unit of speed used by ships

explanation.surface: The bow of a boat rising as it picks up speed on the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' and 'vessel' paint the front of a ship; bow is the ribbon kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a ribbon bow or tuft of hair worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Transformed room with two pieces of lurid gilded stuff

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so the letters are rearranged
only two bits of the following word are taken, its first pair

blocks.note: taken as written
its first two letters

explanation.surface: An interior designer makes over a room with some garish gold decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze or a gold-coloured alloy used to decorate furniture.

clue.text: Company elevated operatic item with introduction of new wind instrument

indicators.note: elevated in a down entry means lifted up, so the word reads upwards
introducing something means putting it in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
an aria is a solo song in an opera
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An opera company improves a number by bringing in a fresh instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Give form to row, omitting last point

indicators.note: omitting the last means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to scull is to row with oars
PT is the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: Shaping an argument by leaving out the final point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel or a line, but is the rowing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To sculpt is to carve or model something into shape, giving it form.

clue.text: Resistance when getting a parking charge

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking; the reversed run inside the word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A motorist objects to being fined for parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking charge' reads as one phrase, a fine; split it, and charge alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap or to beat the rap.

clue.text: Caper the writer's presented in flabby weak conclusion

indicators.note: being presented in something means appearing inside it

blocks.note: an antic is a playful caper
lax means slack or loose
the writer is I, the setter, and 'the writer's' is I am, contracted

explanation.surface: A sloppy author's prank ends feebly.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax is a disappointing let-down after a build-up, a weak ending.

clue.text: Not looking good, using library, overlooking contents

indicators.note: overlooking the contents means ignoring the insides of the words and keeping only their ends

blocks.note: its first and last letters
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A scruffy figure in a library, too busy to notice what is in the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means unattractive in appearance, the opposite of good-looking.

clue.text: Disreputable cut limiting a French book offering little light

indicators.note: a cut word has been shortened, here losing its final letter
to limit is to bound on both sides, so the shortened word encloses the rest

blocks.note: seamy means sordid and disreputable
un is French for a
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A dodgy abridged French book that sheds hardly any light on its subject.
explanation.walkthrough: S(UN + B)EAM: the disreputable word loses its Y and holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a single ray of sunlight, a small amount of light.

clue.text: Prominent statement in court lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter for the following word is taken away

blocks.note: a pleading is a formal statement of a party's case in court
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A notable courtroom statement that lacks force.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading means foremost or principal, as in a leading figure, so prominent.

clue.text: Record no openings for this employee

indicators.note: openings are beginnings, so the initial letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the initials of the two words

explanation.surface: A personnel file noting that there are no vacancies for this worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No openings' reads as one phrase about jobs; 'no' is taken whole and only 'openings for' does the selecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to record it in writing, as in noting down a number.

clue.text: For dispensing, try a cheapo chemist

indicators.note: dispensing means dealing out, so these letters are handed out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Advice to go to a cut-price pharmacy for prescriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispensing' fits the chemist picture perfectly, which hides its role as the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was the old name for a pharmacist who prepared and sold medicines.
